answer: Agents can gate valuable actions behind a bond that is locked until a randomly selected set of counterparties completes independent, costly tasks and confirms the agent behaved consistently. A fake identity must post its own bond and recruit real counterparties, so multiplying accounts multiplies capital at risk rather than influence. In a tundra trade network, a harbor operator might require violet-tagged shipments to clear this check before payment. The attacker pays in locked funds, coordination, and time, and loses the bond when evidence shows collusion or fraud.
